CRDS table management with upsert, expiry, eviction, peer sampling, and gossip updates.

# Purpose
This file implements the CRDS state manager for gossip data. It defines the internal `fd_crds_entry_t` and `fd_crds_purged_t` records, then builds the storage and index structures that the CRDS uses to manage values by key, by hash, by eviction priority, and by expiration time. The code uses generated pool, treap, map, and doubly linked list templates to store active entries, purged hashes, and contact-info side data. It also defines the key hash and key compare logic for gossip value types such as `FD_GOSSIP_VALUE_CONTACT_INFO`, `FD_GOSSIP_VALUE_VOTE`, `FD_GOSSIP_VALUE_EPOCH_SLOTS`, `FD_GOSSIP_VALUE_DUPLICATE_SHRED`, and `FD_GOSSIP_VALUE_NODE_INSTANCE`.

The file also provides the main CRDS API for allocation, join, insertion, eviction, expiration, duplicate detection, and peer sampling. Functions such as [`fd_crds_new`](<#fd_crds_new>), [`fd_crds_join`](<#fd_crds_join>), [`fd_crds_insert`](<#fd_crds_insert>), [`fd_crds_advance`](<#fd_crds_advance>), [`fd_crds_checks_fast`](<#fd_crds_checks_fast>), and [`fd_crds_peer_sample`](<#fd_crds_peer_sample>) manage the life cycle of gossip values and update peer sampler state and metrics. For contact-info entries, the code keeps extra lists for fresh and evict tracking, publishes gossip update messages, and supports peer active or inactive state changes. It also exposes iterators over active and purged entries by hash mask for pull request generation and related gossip operations.
